# Cabinetry: physical model and validation

**Status: simulation-tested engineering model; real-world force/mass calibration remains unverified.**

The package contains 14 hinged doors and four sliding drawers. It builds on the supplied Blender cabinetry_shell exports, preserving the profiled fronts, sink cutouts, fixed shelves and stemware rack. Source files are not overwritten. `mjcf/sink_run.xml`, `mjcf/rear_run.xml`, and `mjcf/prep_run.xml` are independent standalone runs. `mjcf/cabinets.xml` is the standalone assembled kitchen cabinetry, with additional cross-run contacts. Each compiler resolves `meshes/` and `textures/` relative to its XML file. All authored object/default names have `cabinets_` prefixes; the requested keyframe is `rest`.

## Design evidence and decisions

Inputs are `../../assets/cabinetry_shell/{sink_run,rear_run,prep_run}/model.json`, exported OBJ meshes, `../../layout/{structure,parts}.json`, and the supplied constrained articulation embedded in each model. A complete numeric input snapshot is `evidence/measurements.json`. During this task the upstream exporter was concurrently revised using multiview front fits. The final build freezes that newer revision, including its fitted boxes/fronts and all required meshes/textures, in `evidence/source_asset/` and `evidence/fitted_layout.json`; `source_revision.json` lists source hashes. `original_measurements.json` retains the initial annotations for audit. The build never reads changing live meshes after this snapshot. Source frame review included f1035 and f1577 (open upper doors and visible compact concealed cup hinges), f3845 and f3818 (drawer and utensils), f3309 (prep front), and f3684/f3736 (sink fronts).

The doors have older profiled wooden faces, knobs and concealed cup hinges. No identifiable hydraulic damper, soft-close logo, magnetic catch or push-to-open mechanism is visible. Accordingly the default has ordinary friction and viscous damping, **zero closing/opening spring, no 15-degree soft-close ramp, zero latch force, and zero automatic pop-open**. This is a conservative hardware hypothesis, not proof that concealed self-closing springs or dampers are absent. Real hinge testing could require changing it. The hinge axis is a single revolute approximation at the outward panel edge, not a model of a concealed hinge's four-bar linkage.

The drawer frame shows a pale hollow box and utensils, but does not expose enough runner hardware to identify wood, roller or ball bearings. This model selects **wooden runners provisionally**, using higher load-dependent Coulomb friction. The original artist's metal runner detail is not evidence of actual slides and is removed from the moving drawer-box reconstruction. No unsupported ball-bearing or soft-close claim is made.

Manufacturer cross-checks: [Blum COMPACT](https://www.blum.com/us/en/products/hingesystems/compact/programme/) documents face-frame cup hinges at 105, 107 and 110 degrees. That supports a 105-degree hardware prior; it does not identify this kitchen's hinge. [Blum's COMPACT 38N specification](https://d2.blum.com/services/BEC003/concealedhinges_ep_dok_bus_%24sen-us_%24aof_%24v17.pdf) gives a maximum 3/4-inch door thickness for that specific model. Our inherited 20 mm door assumption is about 0.95 mm thicker, so **this is not claimed to be a 38N-compatible replica**. [Knape & Vogt's slide catalogue](https://knapeandvogt.com/sites/default/files/OL2178%20Drawer%20Slides%20Overview%20Brochure%200222.pdf) documents 3/4-extension hardware, including roller types. It supports the extension ratio only, not the selected friction or runner identity. Product load ratings are not product masses or pull forces. For a knob-size comparison, [Amerock Radius BP3686426](https://www.amerock.com/radius-cabinet-knob-bp3686426) specifies a 32 mm diameter, 27 mm projection and 0.19 lb (86.2 g) weight. Our 32 mm spherical grasp proxy and inherited approximately 25 mm handle offset are comparable in size, but the 55 g knob mass is a lighter engineering assumption, not that product weight. The actual knob construction/model remains unidentified.

The [USDA Wood Handbook](https://www.fpl.fs.usda.gov/documnts/fplgtr/fplgtr112.pdf) is the material-property reference for wood density variability; the numerical densities below are engineering priors for unknown wood/composites, not species identification or weighing. No manufacturer/model number or measured weight was available for these installed doors, drawers or knobs. **No real product weights or real handle-force measurements were obtained.**

## Metric frame and geometry corrections

All quantities use metres, kilograms, seconds, newtons and radians. Each run's origin is the bottom centre of corrected rest-state visual bounds, with +Z up. `build_report.json/run_registration` gives the translation back into supplied WORLD; no yaw is applied. The combined model is also recentered at its own bottom centre. Use one combined model or the three registered individual runs, not both.

Source scale is depth-derived `0.16325949132442474 m/reconstruction-unit`, reported approximately 4% uncertainty and not independently verified with a tape measure. A cached measurement CLI depth check at the top-drawer handle pixel f3279 (490, 541.68), in `evidence/handle_depth_check.json`, returned WORLD (-0.406356, 0.214184, 0.831284) m. The initial annotation's grasp point is (-0.3724, 0.2091, 0.8380) m, including an assumed 25 mm protrusion. The approximately 35 mm difference is consistent with depth sampling versus a grasp-point assumption, **not an independent scale validation**.

All dimensional settings are in `params.py/PARAMS`; source coordinates and box sizes are in `PARAMS['measurements']`, while exported source mesh coordinates are scaled exactly once. Set `PARAMS['scale']` and rebuild to apply a future global scale calibration. Frozen source meshes, geometry offsets, drawer travel and render registration scale uniformly. Wood masses scale as s³, geometric inertias as s⁵. Knob hardware and payload kg remain physical masses, so their inertias scale as s². Force/torque priors, gravity, angles and solver tolerances remain fixed SI values; drawer friction is recomputed from loaded mass. Recalibrate forces after a scale change and rerun tests; test acceptance tolerances are fixed physical tolerances, not scaled.

The source independently fitted rectangles, carcasses and axes were inconsistent. Repairs straighten panel planes and joint axes to the corresponding cabinet frame (vertical hinges, horizontal drawers), clip fronts to their parent bounds, separate paired doors by a 3 mm gap, divide drawer fronts at height midplanes to prevent clipping-induced overlaps, trim the sink-right hinge edge against the perpendicular run's corner reveal, and divide overlaps between adjacent upper carcasses at the overlap midpoint with a 3 mm seam. This avoids fictitious gravity torques from depth-fit tilt. The outward-edge hinge pivot keeps the leaf's thickness from sweeping backwards into adjacent stiles. Door widths/heights and displacements are recorded per part in `build_report.json/corrections`; these repairs are explicitly model fits, not new measurements.

Uncovered front strips now have fixed 18 mm face-frame panels. Larger uncovered end regions on the sink/prep run use fixed blind-corner filler. Their extents are derived from the carcass envelope minus measured leaf openings; **their hidden construction and fixation are assumed**. No additional moving leaf was invented. Front profiles and slab geometry remain inherited, with affine corrections to profiled moving fronts. Drawer boxes are rebuilt square, with an open top, separated bottom/sides/back and clearance under the top panel. Source visual wood color is reused in `mjcf/textures/wood.png`; planar UVs, uniform ivory interiors and spherical metal knob contacts are simplified rendering/contact approximations, not preserved full Blender PBR fidelity.

The source sink-door mass was about 21.5 kg because the earlier builder used a world-axis bounding-box volume for rotated panel collision objects. This build uses local material dimensions and analytic solid-body mass properties instead. Door mass = corrected width × height × 0.020 m × 650 kg/m³ + 0.055 kg knob. The door profile is approximated by a uniform 20 mm slab for inertia. Drawer mass includes the 20 mm front, hollow box wall volumes, knob and explicitly assumed contents. Fixed structures use the actual convex box-piece volumes. Drawer side/back/bottom volumes are nonoverlapping; a single filled drawer hull is never used.

## Joint, latch, contact and numerical parameters

| Parameter | Hinged doors | Sliding drawers | Physical/numerical reason |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| frictionloss | 0.22 N·m | 0.25 × loaded mass × 9.81 N | Hinge pin drag prior; dry wood runner prior. Static and sliding bounds equal in MuJoCo. |
| damping | 0.12 N·m·s/rad | 6 N·s/m | Dissipation prior; modest hinge drag / drawer drag. Not identified from video. |
| armature | 0.0002 kg·m² | 0.02 kg | Small reflected hinge/runner inertia regularization. Not an electric motor. |
| stiffness; springref | 0; 0 rad | 0; 0 m | No verified spring law. Passive open parts stay where friction stops them. |
| lower stop | 0 rad | 0 m | Closed mechanical endpoint |
| nominal upper stop | 1.832595715 rad (105°) | 0.75 × box depth | Manufacturer-family plausibility; endpoints assumed |
| solreflimit | 0.006 s, 1 | 0.006 s, 1 | Critically damped soft travel stops; three times contact time constant |
| solimplimit | 0.95 0.99 0.001 0.5 2 | same | Limit impedance range, width, midpoint and power; 0.001 is rad for hinges / m for sliders |
| solreffriction | 0.006 s, 1 | same | Smoothed dry-friction constraint response |
| solimpfriction | 0.95 0.99 0.001 0.5 2 | same | Friction constraint regularization |

All endpoint stops are joint limit constraints, supplemented by genuine body contacts. There are no equality locks, no motor servos, and no buttons, detents, release sensors or opening springs because none were evidenced. `rest` sets every q and velocity to zero. The tests pull shut and release; they do not claim a door will self-close from open.

| Contact setting | Value | Basis |
|---|---|---|
| Wood / general friction | 0.45, 0.005 m, 0.0001 m | Sliding, torsional, rolling Coulomb coefficients; assumed dry surfaces |
| Knob / grasp friction | 0.8, 0.01 m, 0.0002 m | Assumed rubber-gripper/metal effective contact; not metal-on-metal |
| Optional catch friction | 0.5, 0.005 m, 0.0001 m | Assumed; explicit catch pair is normal-only |
| condim | 4 (normal + tangential + torsion) | Rolling coefficient stored but inactive at condim=4 |
| contact solref | 0.002 s, 1 | Critically damped; tuned after the 100 g drop exposed excessive penetration |
| contact solimp | 0.95 0.99 0.001 0.5 2 | Impedance at small/large distance, 1 mm transition width, midpoint/power |
| margin/gap | 0 / 0 normally; catch 0.0002 / 0.0002 m | Catch detection shell uses an inactive contact band; attraction only on detected pad/striker contacts |

Catch provision: each door has a massless fixed child `*_catch_body` containing only a spherical catch pad and an explicit pair with its fixed striker. The MuJoCo `adhesion` actuator is body-based, not geom-based, so this isolation prevents a handle/robot/shelf contact from becoming adhesive. `gain=0 N` in the default model because no catch was identified. `ctrlrange="0 1"`; keyframe `rest` fixes every adhesion control at **1**. Loading a model without resetting the keyframe leaves MuJoCo controls at zero; integrations must call `mj_resetDataKeyframe` or set them explicitly. Controls alone never latch when gain is zero. If real hardware warrants a catch, set the nonnegative `PARAMS["latch"]["force_N"]`, rebuild, and calibrate breakaway at the handle. The test temporarily uses 4 N gain, demonstrates holding under 0.1 N and release under 8 N, and verifies zero generalized actuator force after separation. This is a functional calibration provision, not evidence that the actual cabinet contains magnets.

Gravity is (0, 0, −9.81) m/s². Timestep = 0.001 s; Newton solver, 100 iterations, tolerance 1e−10; `implicitfast`; energy enabled; parent filtering disabled so attached fixed structure is not silently ignored. Visual geoms have zero collision masks and zero mass. Collision boxes and knob spheres have zero geom mass because explicit analytic body inertials own mass. Fixed shells are anchored, not floating. Fixed-to-fixed structural intersections do not produce MuJoCo contacts; the no-penetration claim applies to active collision pairs and does not certify every static join is a disjoint CAD solid.

Inertia is calculated in each body frame from rotated box tensors and the parallel-axis theorem: Ibox = m/12 diag(y²+z², x²+z², x²+y²). Knobs use a solid sphere, I = 2mr²/5. The weighted COM is recomputed across panel, box, knob and payload pieces. Body inertia tensors are positive definite and retain off-diagonal terms in MJCF `fullinertia`. Anchored fixed-body masses are recorded for accounting; they do not accelerate in this fixed-base installation.

## Executed validation

MuJoCo 3.5.0: **PASS**, 9 test methods, 73.386 s measured wall time. JSON contains every force/travel trace, failure list, tested-XML SHA-256 and per-joint results. This is offline simulation execution timing; it excludes reconstruction, build, coding and real-world measurement.

Every force trial applies `xfrc_applied` to the moving body with world force F and COM moment (handle − COM) × F. Hinge force direction follows the instantaneous handle tangent. No direct joint torques or position actuators drive the tested doors/drawers. The force controller limits opening speed and then presses against real contacts/stops. Every integration step checks finite states and penetration. Free probe placement initializes only the new dropped object after force-opening the drawer.

A 0.1 kg, 15 mm-radius free sphere is dropped 150 mm above the top-drawer payload-centre height after force-opening the drawer. It settles on the actual bottom contact geom; maximum penetration across opening/drop is **0.561 mm**. The earlier 6 ms contact response allowed about 3.97 mm penetration; reducing it to 2 ms fixed this failure. Other drawers have checked free cavity centres, but loose-object drops were physically simulated only in the top drawer.

All 18 joints additionally pass a damping ablation: dry friction is set to zero in a temporary model, a handle pulse provides initial velocity, then the damped kinetic-energy ratio is compared with the same trial at zero damping. Every damped ratio is below 0.97 after 0.5 s; the undamped control remains within 0.2% of its initial energy. Default-friction decay trials lose at least 95% of initial kinetic energy within 1 s. Rest drifts/pop-open stay below 1e−5 rad/m, with no numeric warning or NaN. Nonzero springs/push releases were not invented merely to produce a pop-open angle.

## Isaac transfer

`isaac/actuators.py` supplies actual `ImplicitActuatorCfg` construction for **Isaac Lab 2.2.1, Isaac Sim >=5.0, PhysX**. It takes all dry friction, viscous friction and armature values from the same build registry. Passive drives have stiffness=0 and drive damping=0; `viscous_friction` owns damping, avoiding double-counting. Static/dynamic friction are equal effort values. Backend/version guards reject older dimensionless-friction conventions. See the [pinned Isaac actuator configuration API](https://isaac-sim.github.io/IsaacLab/v2.2.1/_modules/isaaclab/actuators/actuator_cfg.html) and [backend friction-convention notes](https://github.com/isaac-sim/IsaacLab/blob/develop/docs/source/concepts/actuators.rst).

The torch contact-catch wrench requires an actual pair-filtered pad/striker contact mask, applies force at the pad and converts to COM torque; it cannot attract on an angle test alone. Default force=0. No custom spring/button actuator is needed for the evidenced mechanisms. Solver stop parameters cannot be copied numerically into PhysX; set the same limits and revalidate stop compliance/contact penetration there. Two torch/config-data unit tests pass, but **Isaac Lab/Isaac Sim are not installed, and no Isaac runtime or USD-import validation was performed**. This file is a tested math/configuration transfer aid, not a certified cross-engine implementation.

## Rebuild and inspect

From this folder, using the supplied simulation Python (or Python with MuJoCo 3.5.0, numpy, scipy, trimesh, Pillow and torch):

```bash
python build.py
python tests/test_physics.py
python tests/test_isaac.py
MUJOCO_GL=egl python render_review.py
python write_physics.py
```

Load an XML and call `mujoco.mj_resetDataKeyframe(model, data, 0)`, followed by `mj_forward`. The individual MJCFs only need their adjacent meshes/textures to load. Rebuilding uses the frozen meshes and numeric measurements in evidence/ and requires no access to the changing upstream asset directory. `review.jpg` shows rest, half-open and force-open installed poses, closeups, signed force/travel loops and release-energy traces. Half-open and closeup poses are inspection states, not a recovered source-video instant. `renders/states.json` records exact rendered qpos and timing.

## Remaining real-world validation

Before claiming sim-to-real behavior, obtain one independent metric reference for the scale job; identify runner/hinge/catch hardware; measure representative door and loaded drawer masses; record quasistatic handle breakaway and running force in both directions at several positions; and capture free-release trajectories and actual installed endpoints. Fit friction, viscous drag and any short-range hinge spring/catch only to those measurements. Contents, compliant wood joints, hinge four-bar kinematics, structural flex, robot fingertip material and unmodeled surrounding appliances can change the result. Tests establish stable behavior under the tested loads and poses; they do not establish measured physical equivalence.

The separate simultaneous-assembly trial pulls all 18 handles together and then releases them. Its maximum penetration is 0.201 mm. Final angles can be smaller than independent installed limits because multiple doors contact one another; exact settled joint positions are saved in tests/results.json.
